---
title: Search Webpages
---

SearcherKit provides a web search pipeline for agents to answer questions about web pages, with the config `web_search`. It searches the public web through
Google Serper and read result pages through Jina Reader. The LLM selects
queries and URLs, then synthesizes an answer from visited evidence.

```bash
question -> LLM -> search -> Serper results
                -> visit  -> Jina Reader page text
                -> LLM -> final answer
```

To use it, you should 
- Abtain API keys for required services
- Configure enviroment variables for LLM and file search root
- Run searchagent tui with the `web_search` config.

### Install SearcherKit

SearcherKit requires Python 3.12 or later. Install the package in a virtual
environment:

:::: {.panel-tabset}
#### pip

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install searcherkit
```

#### uv

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
uv pip install searcherkit
```
::::

##### Prepare required services

Prepare an LLM endpoint, a [Serper](https://serper.dev/) API key, and optionally
a Jina Reader API key. The machine must be able to reach the LLM endpoint,
`google.serper.dev`, and `r.jina.ai`.

### Configure the environment

SearcherKit with `web_search` config take the following enviroment variables.

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model name sent to the endpoint |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | LLM endpoint credential |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible API base URL |
| `SERPER_API_KEY` | Required credential for web search |
| `JINA_API_KEY` | Optional credential for Jina Reader |

For a one-time setup, define the variables in the terminal session where you
will start SearcherKit. The values remain available until that terminal is
closed.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Bash

```bash
export LLM_MODEL="YOUR_MODEL"
export LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export LLM_BASE_URL="https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
export SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
export JINA_API_KEY="YOUR_JINA_API_KEY"
```

#### PowerShell

```powershell
$env:LLM_MODEL = "YOUR_MODEL"
$env:LLM_API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
$env:LLM_BASE_URL = "https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
$env:SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
$env:JINA_API_KEY="YOUR_JINA_API_KEY"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
To keep the configuration across terminal sessions, create a `.env` file in
the directory where you run SearcherKit:

```bash
LLM_MODEL=YOUR_MODEL
LLM_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY
LLM_BASE_URL=https://your-endpoint.example/v1
SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
JINA_API_KEY="YOUR_JINA_API_KEY"
```

SearcherKit loads `.env` by default. Use `--env-file path/to/another.env` to load a
different file. Variables already defined in the terminal take precedence over
values in the dotenv file. 
:::

### Start the TUI

```bash
searcher tui --config-path web_search
```

Type `/` in the TUI to view available commands. Use `/tool-detail` to inspect tool arguments and results. For general controls and record behavior, see [Use the Interactive TUI](../04-interface/02-use-the-interactive-tui.qmd).

Interactive records, the global log, and trace logs are written under
`outputs/file-search-tui/interactive`.

For the complete source/tool guidance, see [Sources and Tools](../03-customizing/03-sources-and-tools.qmd).


### Common failuares and solutions

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| 401 or 403 from search | `SERPER_API_KEY` and account permissions |
| 401 or 403 while visiting | `JINA_API_KEY` or Jina access policy |
| Model rejects tool calls | Model chat template and server tool-call parser |
| Timeout or connection failure | Endpoint URL, DNS, proxy, firewall, and service health |
